GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Join us to turn ideas into world-changing realities where every voice matters and every difference builds a healthier world. Make a real-world impact through hands-on experience.

Job Description

Are you passionate about electrical engineering and eager to gain hands-on experience in a world-class lab environment? As an Electrical Engineering Co-op at GE HealthCare, you’ll work alongside engineers and technicians on high-impact projects that support the development of cutting-edge CT scanner technologies.

This 12-month co-op is designed to give you exposure to real-world challenges and prepare you for a future career in electrical engineering or product development. You’ll be part of the premium CT hardware engineering team, contributing to solutions that improve quality, reduce costs, and enhance patient care.

As a Co-op, you’ll take on project-based assignments with mentorship and training from experienced engineers. You’ll gain skills in electrical technician work and contribute to initiatives that support innovation and operational excellence. Looking for a well-rounded Electrical technical student that can execute on a variety of tasks on this super-awesome fun-tastic team.

Key Responsibilities

You’ll work on a variety of hands-on tasks, including:

- Soldering, assembling prototypes, and building test fixtures
- Setting up and running data acquisition equipment for testing
- Using electrical test equipment (DMMs, oscilloscopes, power supplies, network analyzers, etc.) to evaluate new designs
- Documenting test results and troubleshooting electrical systems
- Prototyping, reworking, and designing circuits to improve CT scanner performance
- Conducting experiments and diagnostic tests to support root cause analysis
- Evaluating software and hardware and implementing improvements
- Communicating technical findings to improve system performance and reliability
- Supporting the development of engineering, manufacturing, and service documentation
- Complying with Environment Health and Safety (EHS) regulations and quality policies

Qualifications

We’re looking for students who are ready to learn, lead, and make a difference. You are:

- Currently enrolled full-time in a technical diploma or degree program (pursuing Associate’s or Bachelor’s) in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field
- Available to work a minimum of 20 hours/week during spring/fall semesters or 40 hours/week during summer
- Able to work onsite at our Waukesha, WI facility
- Legally authorized to work in the U.S. (we do not sponsor employment visas for this role)

Preferred Qualifications

You may stand out if you have:

- Experience in mechanical or electrical trades
- Familiarity with Cadence or other ECAD software
- Basic understanding of a programming language such as Matlab
- Familiarity with digital electronics, switches and/or flux capacitors
- Strong communication skills and ability to simplify technical concepts
- Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills
- Proven leadership and initiative in academic or extracurricular settings
- Passion for technology and continuous learning
- A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (on a 4.0 scale)

Why Join Us?

At GE HealthCare, we’re building a healthier world powered by innovation and collaboration. As an Electrical Engineering Co-op, you’ll gain hands-on experience, mentorship, and exposure to a global organization that values inclusion, integrity, and impact.

We offer competitive compensation and a culture that supports learning, growth, and real-world contributions.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening.

Additional Information

GE HealthCare offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE HealthCare will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

About the Role

Invitation Homes set out to solve a real problem: home leasing options were limited and the experience for renters was inconsistent. Today, as the nation’s largest single-family home rental company, our engineering teams build the technology at the center of that solution: personalized resident experiences, service tools, and the operational systems that residents and associates depend on every day. When we ship, people feel it.

Our paid summer internship is a first step toward a career in software engineering. You’ll join a real team for about ten weeks, work on a scoped project, and ship something that matters. Along the way you’ll have a manager and an assigned mentor who are invested in your growth, plus intern events, community outreach, and an executive speaker series.

This role maps to the learning side of what many organizations call an entry-level Software Engineer. You’re a hands-on learner from day one. The goal is to leave with real experience, real relationships, and a clear sense of what engineering looks like here.

What You’ll Do

Technical Leadership

· Work on a well-scoped project that contributes to your team’s goals, with support from your mentor.

· Write code, fix bugs, and ship small changes to production.

· Follow your team’s established patterns and conventions; ask when you’re unsure why they exist.

· Join standups, sprint planning, and retrospectives as a full member of the team.

Knowledge & Standards

· Learn your team’s core tools and technologies: what they are, why we use them, and how to use them well.

· Write automated tests alongside your code, and work with quality assurance on anything that needs manual testing.

· Treat every task as a chance to learn something new.

Communication & Collaboration

· Ask for help early and often. It’s expected.

· Ask clarifying questions before diving in, and check in with your mentor regularly.

· Write clear pull request descriptions, and read your teammates’ pull requests to learn from them.

· Seek out feedback and use it.

· Present what you built to your team at the end of the internship.

Leadership & Culture

· Show up consistently, stay curious, and be coachable.

· Take part in intern events and engineering community forums, and get to know people across the department.

What You Bring

· A rising senior pursuing a bachelor’s degree at an accredited four-year university in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

· An expected graduation date between December and May following the internship.

· Foundational programming knowledge in at least one language, with a desire to build on it.

· Eagerness to learn, and openness to feedback.

· The ability to work as a self-starter and to prioritize your work with a sense of urgency.

· A willingness to collaborate with teammates and ask good questions.

Our Stack

Our engineering teams work with TypeScript, Node.js, React, PostgreSQL, and AWS, including Lambda, DynamoDB, and RDS. We practice CI/CD, favor infrastructure as code, and build on REST APIs and event-driven architectures. Salesforce and Yardi are significant parts of our technology landscape: some teams build directly on these platforms, while others integrate with their APIs. Experience with any of these is a plus, but we care more about curiosity, adaptability, and the drive to keep learning than familiarity with any specific tool.

Salary Range

$17.90 - $31.03

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, Veteran status or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state or local law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please contact us at humanresources@invitationhomes.com.

About Fervo Energy

Fervo Energy (NASDAQ: FRVO) is a modern power company developing next-generation geothermal resources to meet the growing demand for affordable, reliable, 24/7 carbon-free energy. Our mission is to transform geothermal into America’s most dependable and affordable source of clean, around-the-clock power. By combining innovations in horizontal drilling, fiber-optic sensing, and advanced reservoir engineering, Fervo has developed a repeatable approach to building utility-scale enhanced geothermal systems. Our flagship Cape Station development in Utah is planned to deliver 500 MW of firm, carbon-free power, and we are advancing a development pipeline of more than 50 GW. Join us and work alongside world-class engineers, geoscientists, operators, project builders, and business leaders working to make geothermal a cornerstone of a more reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy future.

Internship Overview

You won't be running coffee orders or shuffling paperwork this summer. At Fervo, interns are handed something real: a project of your own, scoped with your manager on day one and yours to drive for the full 12 weeks. You'll work side-by-side with the teams building the next generation of geothermal energy, tackling problems that genuinely move the business forward. At the end of the summer, you'll present your work to our executive leadership team, department leads, and fellow interns, sharing real results with a real audience. This is a real seat at the table — and a real shot at what comes next.

Position Description

As our GIS Intern, you’ll join the GIS team out of our Salt Lake City office and support the spatial data backbone behind Fervo’s geothermal resource development. Geothermal projects live and die on geospatial context — where the heat is, where the land rights are, where the wells and infrastructure can go — and you’ll help our geoscientists, land team, and engineers see and use that context clearly.

You’ll build and maintain the maps, layers, and spatial datasets that inform site selection, permitting, and field development decisions, and you’ll have the chance to bring automation and scripting into workflows that are still done by hand. Your work will directly shape how the team visualizes and reasons about the subsurface resources that power Fervo’s next projects.

Responsibilities

- Build, maintain, and QC GIS layers covering lease and land boundaries, well pads, transmission corridors, and subsurface resource targets

- Support resource characterization by integrating geologic, geophysical, and land datasets into spatial models used across the Geoscience and Land teams

- Produce maps, figures, and spatial visualizations for internal technical reviews, permitting submissions, and field development planning

- Help automate recurring spatial data workflows (e.g., using Python/ArcPy) to reduce manual data handling and improve data quality

- Partner with geoscience, land, and engineering colleagues to support site selection, due diligence, and project siting decisions

Qualifications

Required

- Rising Junior, Senior, Master’s candidate wrapping up within the next year, or PhD candidate — we’re building a pipeline toward full-time offers

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting to stakeholders and leadership

- Eagerness to learn, take initiative, and adapt quickly to new challenges

- Pursuing a degree in GIS, Geography, Geology, Environmental Science, or a related field, with hands-on experience in ArcGIS Pro and/or QGIS and core spatial analysis concepts [Hiring manager: confirm/adjust role-specific requirements]

Preferred

- Knowledge in PLSS System

- Knowledge in Esri Products, Enterprise is a plus

Location

Fervo Energy has offices in Houston, TX, Golden, CO, Reno, NV, Oakland, CA, and Salt Lake City, UT. This position will be eligible for some hybrid work flexibility, but regular in-office presence in Salt Lake City, Utah will be required.

Benefits & Perks

- Fervo offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work. Benefits for eligible employees include:

- Medical, dental, and vision plan options

- Employer-paid basic life insurance and short-term and long-term disability coverage

- Employee ownership opportunities through Fervo’s Employee Stock Purchase Program, as well as LTI and bonus opportunities for eligible roles

Benefits and programs are subject to eligibility requirements and may change.

Our Workplace

Fervo Energy highly values having employees work in the office to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. This role follows a hybrid schedule, with team members expected to work in the office three days per week. Fervo considers this in-office schedule an essential function of the role. About Valstad

Valstad is building the machine that builds the ships.

We combine industrial robotics, welding, sensing, and AI to turn 3D models into real high-mix ship structure. Our mission is to rapidly expand America's maritime output by 100x.

Our team works directly with large industrial robots and real manufacturing equipment at our Austin facility. The systems we build will ultimately be deployed across shipyards and industrial facilities throughout the country.

About Valstad

Valstad is rebuilding how ships are made.

American shipbuilding is constrained by slow, labor-intensive production methods and a shortage of skilled manufacturing capacity. We are developing robotic production systems that can turn engineering data directly into finished steel structures, dramatically reducing the time and manual programming required to build ships.

Our first platform combines industrial robots, automated material handling, welding, sensing and AI-driven manufacturing software to produce large ship panels and structural assemblies. Instead of programming each new part by hand, our goal is for the system to understand the CAD model, determine how the structure should be assembled and welded, and generate the robotic plan required to build it.

Achieving that requires solving difficult robotics problems involving kinematics, coordinate frames, motion planning, simulation, calibration, collision checking, sensor integration and execution on real industrial hardware.

The software you build will be tested against full-scale industrial robots in our Austin facility, not only in simulation.

The Internship

Valstad is seeking a Robotics Software Intern to work on manipulation, motion-planning, simulation or robot-verification software.

You will own a defined technical project that improves the reliability, performance or diagnosability of Valstad’s robotic manufacturing systems. Depending on your background and our current priorities, you may work on planning algorithms, simulation infrastructure, coordinate-frame visualization, calibration analysis, robot-log replay or automated path verification.

This is not a shadowing program or a collection of disconnected research tasks. You will be expected to implement, test and document a working capability that can become part of Valstad’s robotics platform.

You will work closely with a robotics engineer and will receive structured mentorship, code review and access to real robotic systems.

Potential Projects

Your primary project will be selected based on your experience and Valstad’s highest-priority technical needs. Possible projects include:

- Building a motion-planning regression-test suite using representative manufacturing scenarios

- Developing tools for visualizing coordinate frames, transforms, robot poses and calibration results

- Generating reachability maps for robots mounted on linear rails

- Testing inverse-kinematics continuity along long Cartesian paths

- Detecting singularities, wrist flips, joint-limit conditions and trajectory discontinuities

- Creating automated collision-checking and path-validation scenarios

- Building a robot-log replay system for reproducing hardware failures in simulation

- Comparing commanded, simulated and physically executed robot trajectories

- Developing cycle-time prediction and trajectory-analysis tools

- Evaluating planning algorithms for constrained welding or scanning paths

- Building tools for calibration-data analysis and error visualization

- Supporting integration of a laser scanner, camera, force sensor or other non-safety-critical device

- Developing simulation models for robots, fixtures, tools and workpieces

- Improving visualization of robot work envelopes, collision geometry and external axes

- Creating automated pre-execution checks for generated robot programs

What You Will Do

- Design and implement a scoped robotics-software project.

- Work with rust, Python or both.

- Use simulation and recorded data to test your work.

- Work with rigid-body transformations, robot kinematics and 3D geometry where relevant.

- Build automated tests for nominal and failure scenarios.

- Participate in robotics architecture discussions and code reviews.

- Analyze logs and robot behavior to diagnose planning or execution issues.

- Validate your work using real robotic hardware when appropriate and under supervision.

- Document assumptions, algorithms, interfaces and limitations.

- Present your results and demonstrate the completed capability to the Valstad team.

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral degree in robotics, computer science, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, aerospace engineering or a related field.

- Strong programming fundamentals.

- Experience with Python, rust or both.

- Coursework or practical experience in linear algebra, three-dimensional geometry, kinematics, dynamics, controls or motion planning.

- Experience completing a meaningful robotics, software or research project.

- Ability to reason about technical systems and debug unexpected behavior.

- Ability to work independently within a defined project scope.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Interest in robotic manipulation and real-world industrial systems.

- Availability to work full-time and on-site in Austin for the duration of the internship.

Strongly Preferred

- Strong rust experience.

- Experience with ROS or ROS 2.

- Experience with MoveIt, Tesseract, OMPL, Drake, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Gazebo or another robotics framework.

- Experience with forward and inverse kinematics.

- Experience with homogeneous transformations, quaternions and coordinate-frame conventions.

- Experience with collision detection or motion planning.

- Experience working with robotic manipulators.

- Experience with Eigen, NumPy or similar numerical libraries.

- Experience developing simulation or verification tools.

- Experience with industrial robot arms, linear rails or external axes.

- Experience with robot calibration, hand-eye calibration or sensor localization.

- Experience working with cameras, laser scanners, force-torque sensors or other robotics hardware.

- Participation in a robotics laboratory, student robotics team, Formula SAE, combat robotics or relevant open-source project.

What We Look For

We value evidence that you can apply robotics concepts to systems that behave imperfectly outside the laboratory.

Strong candidates often have:

- A manipulator or hardware project they can explain in depth

- Research involving real robot experiments

- Open-source robotics contributions

- Experience debugging coordinate-frame or calibration problems

- Simulation work connected to physical validation

- A clear understanding of the difference between an algorithm working once and a system operating reliably

You do not need industrial-robot or shipbuilding experience. We care more about robotics fundamentals, software quality and an interest in making algorithms work on physical machines.

Safety and Production Boundaries

Interns may work with industrial robots under the supervision of qualified Valstad personnel.

Interns will not independently:

- Modify safety systems

- Authorize production releases

- Commission energized equipment without supervision

- Make uncontrolled changes to production robot or PLC programs

- Bypass interlocks, protective devices or established review procedures

Production-facing changes will be reviewed and approved by full-time engineers.

What Success Looks Like

By the end of the internship, you will have delivered a working robotics-software capability that improves planning, simulation, verification or hardware debugging.

Your project will have:

- A clearly defined technical objective

- A tested implementation

- Representative nominal and failure scenarios

- Documentation of assumptions and limitations

- Integration with Valstad’s software or simulation environment where appropriate

- A final demonstration using real robot data or physical hardware

The strongest interns may be considered for future internships or full-time positions.

Compensation and Benefits

The anticipated pay range for this internship is $34 to $42 per hour, depending on experience and technical depth.

The internship also includes:

- A dedicated robotics mentor

- Access to industrial robotic systems

- Ownership of a substantive technical project

- Regular technical feedback and code review

- Potential relocation or temporary-housing assistance where appropriate

- Consideration for future internship or full-time opportunities

WindBorne is looking for a Firmware Intern to build the code bases that runs on our balloon hardware. We believe the most interesting work happens at the intersection of hardware and software, where clever code can compensate for physical limitations. In this role, you’ll design and run experiments to understand the behaviors of our system in weird conditions, then cosplay as a 1960s NASA engineer to glean insight from the limited data available.
